cards.title: Design Product Selection, Bundle Savings, and Add-to-Cart as One Flow
cards.summary: Put product choice near the top, calculate bundle value for the shopper, and confirm add-to-cart without disruptive page reloads.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the purchase area of a PDP, bundle landing page, or campaign page for physical products.

cards.title: Structure a Complete Ecommerce Landing Page Around Decisions
cards.summary: Organize campaign and product landing pages so each section resolves the next shopper uncertainty: relevance, product choice, proof, differentiation, use, risk, and purchase.
cards.use_when: Planning a long-form product landing page, bundle campaign, or collection page that must educate and sell without becoming a generic lead-generation page.

cards.title: Advertorial placement in the funnel
cards.summary: Insert a pre-sell advertorial page between cold prospecting ads and the offer/checkout page to educate and build desire before asking for a sale.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to route paid social or paid search traffic that converts poorly when sent straight to a PDP or offer page.

cards.title: The seven-section advertorial architecture
cards.summary: Sequence advertorials as hook/trust above the fold, skimmable listicle, origin story and unique mechanism, proof story plus social proof, risk reversal, two-options close, and a final CTA.
cards.use_when: Writing or restructuring the section order of an advertorial or long-form pre-sell landing page.

cards.title: Hit the pain threshold, not just a pain point
cards.summary: Stack pain points aggressively until the reader's emotional pain threshold is crossed and they are compelled to act.
cards.use_when: Writing advertorial or PDP copy that agitates a problem but still fails to convert readers who acknowledge the issue.

cards.title: Name and repeat a unique mechanism
cards.summary: Define a specific, named mechanism explaining why the product works when past solutions failed, and reference it throughout the page.
cards.use_when: Selling a product in a category where buyers have tried several competing solutions and are skeptical they'll work.

cards.title: Map pain points and desires before writing
cards.summary: List the 3–5 dominant customer pains and desires up front, then repeat that same set throughout the page in different formats.
cards.use_when: Preparing to write an advertorial or long-form product page and needing a repeatable messaging spine.

cards.title: Order testimonials against specific objections
cards.summary: Structure social proof so each testimonial systematically dismantles one specific buying objection instead of offering generic praise.
cards.use_when: Building the social-proof section of an advertorial, PDP, or offer page where testimonials feel interchangeable and weak.

cards.title: Deploy risk reversals to remove purchase friction
cards.summary: State a strong, low-friction guarantee — extended money-back terms, no-hoops, no questions asked — to eliminate the perceived risk of buying.
cards.use_when: Designing the guarantee and risk-reversal section of an advertorial, offer page, or PDP for a considered-purchase product.

cards.title: Frame CTAs as checking availability, not 'buy now'
cards.summary: Replace pushy 'buy now' buttons with scarcity-framed CTAs like 'apply discount / check availability' to reduce resistance.
cards.use_when: Writing advertorial or offer-page CTA copy where a hard-sell button would feel too aggressive for the audience.

cards.title: Write the 'two options' close
cards.summary: Close by laying out a stay-the-course option versus a risk-free product option, then let the reader conclude the product is the better choice.
cards.use_when: Finishing the close of an advertorial or long-form offer page after the reader has seen the proof and guarantee.

cards.title: Use a point-of-view proof story with before/after arc
cards.summary: Run a long narrative customer story that starts with skepticism, records quick early results, and escalates to a transformed outcome.
cards.use_when: Writing the proof-story section of an advertorial where a short testimonial lacks persuasive depth.

cards.title: Build a fast proof-of-results claim
cards.summary: Reduce time-to-result claims to the first use or first round and quantify cumulative user volume to imply reliability.
cards.use_when: Writing the results section of an advertorial or PDP for a product whose benefit normally takes weeks.

cards.title: Advertorial input-prep: strip the sales page into a clean text PDF once
cards.summary: Convert the sales page or sales letter you want advertorials for into an image-free PDF so it can be attached to AI prompts as the source of truth.
cards.use_when: You are about to produce advertorials (pre-sell articles) for a product page and need a reusable source document of the sales copy.

cards.title: Extract the sales-page input set before writing any advertorial
cards.summary: Run a fixed question battery against the sales-page PDF to pull target market, pain points, promises, proof, common failed solutions, real culprit, product facts and ingredients into one reusable doc.
cards.use_when: Product selection and messaging: you are preparing to write advertorials or ad angles and need the raw claims and audience material extracted first.

cards.title: Split one broad product into avatar archetypes for advertorial variants
cards.summary: Ask the model to propose several audience archetypes from the extracted market data so each advertorial speaks to one specific segment instead of everyone.
cards.use_when: Product selection and creative strategy: you want multiple advertorial versions to test against different cold-traffic segments for the same product.

cards.title: Find live advertorial swipe structures to model
cards.summary: Collect real advertorials from mainstream sites and spy tools to use as structural templates before writing.
cards.use_when: Creative strategy: you need proven advertorial structures to model your ecommerce advertorial on.

cards.title: Advertorial architecture: the repeating section skeleton
cards.summary: Reverse-engineer the standard advertorial flow — problem story, failed solutions, discovery, mechanism, product reveal, proof, CTA — and reproduce it for your product.
cards.use_when: Landing-page and advertorial writing: you are drafting or reviewing an advertorial draft and need the structural spine it should follow.

cards.title: Prompt pattern: model a new advertorial on a swipe plus your input doc
cards.summary: Combine an unrelated advertorial swipe, the extracted sales-page inputs and a chosen avatar into one prompt that produces a full draft in the swipe's style.
cards.use_when: PDP/landing-page work: you need a complete advertorial draft for a specific avatar written fast, in the style of a proven example.

cards.title: Scrub hallucinated spokespeople, studies and prices from AI drafts
cards.summary: Treat every named person, study citation, price and testimonial in an AI advertorial as unverified until checked against the real offer.
cards.use_when: Pre-publish QA on any AI-drafted advertorial or ad before it goes to the offer page.

cards.title: Vary the swipe template as well as the avatar
cards.summary: Produce more advertorial variants by swapping the structural swipe (e.g. a doctor-fronted one) in addition to swapping the avatar.
cards.use_when: Creative testing at scale: you need a larger batch of distinct advertorial variants for one product to feed cold traffic.

cards.title: Advertorial as pre-sell between ad and offer
cards.summary: Use an advertorial when the destination page alone can't carry a cold reader, especially for short ecommerce pages or as a bridge to a long-form sales letter.
cards.use_when: Funnel architecture: deciding whether cold traffic should hit your ecommerce page directly or be routed through an advertorial first.

cards.title: Keep a running outputs doc so later advertorial runs skip re-analysis
cards.summary: Persist the extracted inputs and each finished advertorial in a project document so future runs only need the swipe, the inputs and a new avatar.
cards.use_when: Landing-page production planning: you'll write advertorials for the same product repeatedly over weeks or months.

cards.title: Quiz funnels work by emotionally priming, not just personalizing
cards.summary: The real conversion power of a quiz funnel is putting cold traffic into an emotionally primed, suggestible state through micro-commitments before the offer appears.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to insert a quiz between paid ad traffic and your PDP/sales page, or defending the extra step to stakeholders who think it only adds friction.

cards.title: Every quiz question must commit, seed, or pre-handle
cards.summary: Each question in a quiz funnel should serve one of three jobs: earn a micro-commitment, seed a buying belief, or pre-handle a sales objection.
cards.use_when: Auditing or writing quiz questions before you build the funnel, so you don't pad it with questions that only create drop-off.

cards.title: Keep product-quiz steps easy and visibly responsive
cards.summary: Reduce interaction effort while collecting meaningful product preferences.
cards.use_when: Designing the interaction pattern and answer controls for a quiz funnel that feeds a Shopify PDP.

cards.title: Gradualization: start non-invasive, escalate slowly
cards.summary: Open with questions that are easy and non-personal, then gradually build toward more invasive questions to protect completion.
cards.use_when: Ordering quiz questions, especially when targeting demographics where direct personal questions (age, weight, body issues) would feel rude or intrusive.

cards.title: Seed buying beliefs through reframing questions
cards.summary: Use quiz questions to reframe a symptom as a serious quality-of-life problem, installing the belief that underpins the purchase.
cards.use_when: Writing quiz questions for a health or problem-solving product where the buyer needs to believe the problem is serious before they'll buy.

cards.title: Pre-handle objections inside the quiz, before the offer
cards.summary: Ask questions that neutralize common objections (like 'results take too long') so the objection is defused before the sales page is ever shown.
cards.use_when: Preparing quiz questions for a product with well-known objections (time-to-results, 'I've tried everything', ingredients).

cards.title: Avoid input questions unless deliberately adding friction
cards.summary: Typing answers has far higher perceived effort than tapping choices and causes heavy drop-off, so reserve input questions for deliberate buyer qualification.
cards.use_when: Choosing answer-control types for quiz questions, or deciding whether to keep a free-text question in an existing quiz.

cards.title: Target a ~30% quiz completion rate and diagnose per-question drop-off
cards.summary: Aim for roughly 30% of starters finishing the quiz, and use per-question drop-off data to find and fix the questions costing you the most.
cards.use_when: Setting performance benchmarks for a quiz funnel and reviewing its analytics after launch to optimize completion.

cards.title: Size the quiz: 3–20 questions, sweet spot 8–12
cards.summary: There is a point of diminishing returns on quiz length; keep it roughly 3–20 questions, typically 8–12, and cut any question that doesn't earn its place.
cards.use_when: Deciding how long to make a quiz funnel before writing or building it.

cards.title: Build a quiz with AI on top of foundational customer docs
cards.summary: Generate quiz questions in AI only after uploading an offer doc, avatar doc, research doc, and beliefs doc — then have it analyze a proven example quiz first.
cards.use_when: Drafting quiz questions and copy for a new funnel when you already have (or need to build) customer research assets.

cards.title: Capture name and email at the end to unlock remarketing and email sequences
cards.summary: Require name and email to receive the personalized quiz result, then follow with a 5–7 email sequence — ideally branched by quiz answers.
cards.use_when: Planning the post-quiz step of a funnel to grow a list and drive purchase via email retention flows.

cards.title: Evaluate health niches for quiz funnel inspiration
cards.summary: Look inside the health niche (and similar problem-aware categories) to study high-traffic quiz funnels as models for structure and question sequencing.
cards.use_when: Sourcing quiz funnel examples and structures to adapt for your own store's product category.

cards.title: Treat quiz funnels as a time-limited opportunity, not a permanent channel
cards.summary: The source frames quiz funnels as the current 'funnel architecture' to exploit with urgency, implying you should test and scale quickly rather than wait.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to prioritize building a quiz funnel now versus other acquisition projects, and planning how long to rely on it.

cards.title: Landing page success is a two-metric game
cards.summary: Judge landing pages only by conversion rate and average order value, not by visual aesthetics.
cards.use_when: Auditing a store's PDP, advertorial or sales page before redesigning it, or deciding whether to ship an ugly-but-fast page.

cards.title: Sales page, order page, OTO: route traffic through a response funnel instead of a PDP
cards.summary: Replace the ad-to-PDP-to-checkout flow with a Sales Page, Order Page and sequential post-purchase one-time offers.
cards.use_when: Designing or rebuilding the funnel for a high-AOV direct-to-consumer offer, especially where ad traffic currently lands on a standard product detail page.

cards.title: Post-purchase OTOs exploit peak price elasticity
cards.summary: The moment after payment is the most emotional and most price-elastic point in the customer relationship, so put the biggest upsell there.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much to charge for an upsell and where in the funnel to place the highest-ticket offer.

cards.title: Landing pages are copy plus media plus design - only two carry the sale
cards.summary: Break any landing page into copy, media and design; copy is the main lever and design only matters if it adds friction.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend effort when building or improving a product page, advertorial or sales page.

cards.title: Voice of Customer: write copy in the customer's words using a four-document research set
cards.summary: Produce a research doc, offer brief, avatar sheet and necessary-belief doc from forums and reviews, then write copy from customer language rather than marketer bias.
cards.use_when: Starting copy, angles or ad creative for a new product, or diagnosing why existing page copy does not resonate.

cards.title: Marketing as belief change: define the limiting beliefs you must shift
cards.summary: List the beliefs a visitor currently holds, then design the page to move them from limiting to empowering beliefs.
cards.use_when: Structuring a sales page or ad angle for a skeptical audience, or when conversion stalls despite clear copy.

cards.title: Headline checklist: hit three to four of seven to earn the scroll
cards.summary: Score benefit-driven headlines against seven traits and rewrite until at least three or four are present.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the above-the-fold headline on a sales page, advertorial, PDP or ad landing page.

cards.title: Urgency and scarcity: sell time or sell volume, but do it honestly
cards.summary: Use time-based urgency and supply-based scarcity to prompt action, keeping the claims defensible.
cards.use_when: Designing hero banners, offer sections, shipping cut-offs or promo modules on a sales or order page.

cards.title: Risk reversal: design a guarantee, don't just lengthen one
cards.summary: Make the guarantee remove risk for the buyer rather than compete on duration alone.
cards.use_when: Choosing the guarantee, returns policy or trial offer shown on a sales page or order page.

cards.title: Unique mechanism: explain why everything else failed and yours works
cards.summary: State the specific reason the product works and why prior attempts did not, to make the promise believable.
cards.use_when: Writing the mechanism section of a sales page or the core angle of an ad for a crowded category.

cards.title: Embedded testimonials pre-handle objections before the FAQ
cards.summary: Place purposeful social proof throughout the page to overcome objections or install an empowering belief.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to put customer reviews and testimonials across a sales page or order page.

cards.title: Credibility is market-specific, so research who the market trusts
cards.summary: Choose credibility signals based on what the target market actually respects, not default authority figures.
cards.use_when: Selecting expert endorsements, certifications or founder story elements for a sales page or ad.

cards.title: Order page: minimize friction, then add quantity breaks and order bumps
cards.summary: The order page should be boringly clear, with quantity discounts and cheap checkout bumps doing the AOV work.
cards.use_when: Optimizing the payment step of a funnel, or comparing a custom order page against a default Shopify checkout.

cards.title: OTO page formats: VSL or TSL, with two proven product frameworks
cards.summary: Structure post-purchase offers as a short video or text sales letter, and pick the product with 'more of the same' or 'solve one problem, create another'.
cards.use_when: Building the post-purchase upsell step for a supplement, consumable or consumable-adjacent product.

cards.title: Retire misconceptions: clarity over cleverness, subtraction over design
cards.summary: On high-drop-off pages, enforce clarity and remove confusing elements before adding anything new.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a checkout or sales page that has high traffic but poor completion.

cards.title: Funnel drop-off is a leak map: plug gaps with email and SMS
cards.summary: Every step in the funnel loses people, and owned messaging exists to recover those specific leaks.
cards.use_when: Planning lifecycle email or SMS flows for a store that runs a multi-step sales funnel.

cards.title: Advertorial Fundamentals and the Don't-Rewrite-a-Swipe Rule
cards.summary: What an advertorial is and why asking AI to rewrite a competitor's ad without foundational research produces low-converting copy.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to produce a long-form advertorial landing page for paid traffic rather than a standard product page.

cards.title: The Five-Step AI Advertorial SOP
cards.summary: Overview of the five-stage AI workflow for producing advertorials: research, foundational docs, swipe, draft, chief.
cards.use_when: Planning production capacity for paid-traffic advertorial landing pages and deciding where in the workflow to invest human time.

cards.title: Grounding AI in Your Product Before Prompting
cards.summary: Upload your sales page and existing copy as PDFs so the model writes from real product context instead of generic assumptions.
cards.use_when: Preparing inputs before generating advertorial or landing page copy for a specific product.

cards.title: AI Inception: Making the Model Write Its Own Deep Research Prompt
cards.summary: Prompt ChatGPT to generate the Deep Research prompt itself so the customer research scrape is as comprehensive as possible.
cards.use_when: Running customer research for a new advertorial, new offer or new market entry before writing any landing page copy.

cards.title: Building the Avatar Sheet from AI Research
cards.summary: Convert the raw research document into a structured avatar sheet with demographics, pain points and verbatim customer quotes.
cards.use_when: Creating the audience profile that will drive advertorial messaging, hooks and headline angles for a specific product.

cards.title: The Offer Brief: Funnel Architecture, Awareness and Unique Mechanism
cards.summary: Build an offer document capturing funnel architecture, stage of awareness, sophistication and unique mechanism before drafting copy.
cards.use_when: Preparing to write an advertorial or sales page and needing to pin down what offer, at which stage of awareness, the copy must carry.

cards.title: The Necessary Beliefs Document (Max Six Beliefs)
cards.summary: Define up to six beliefs a prospect must hold to buy, so copy has a checklist of mindset shifts to achieve.
cards.use_when: Structuring advertorial narrative and objection handling around the belief shifts required before a visitor will purchase.

cards.title: Swipe Selection and Structuring an Advertorial Draft
cards.summary: Choose a currently successful competitor advertorial as a structural reference and prompt AI to write your draft in halves.
cards.use_when: Drafting a new advertorial landing page and needing a proven structure plus a workable drafting process.

cards.title: Chiefing: AI Review Against Foundational Docs, Then Human Pass
cards.summary: Edit process where AI checks the draft against research, beliefs and mechanism, then a human removes friction from the read.
cards.use_when: Final review of an advertorial before spending money on paid traffic to that landing page.

cards.title: Slippery Slide Editing: Finding and Removing Bumps
cards.summary: Practical editing pass for advertorial copy that locates friction points where the reader might stop sliding toward the CTA.
cards.use_when: Line-level editing of advertorial or landing page copy before launch to paid traffic.

cards.title: Driving Traffic to an Advertorial with Open-Loop Headlines
cards.summary: Use curiosity-driven, unresolved headlines in advertorials so paid traffic clicks through and reads rather than bouncing.
cards.use_when: Writing the headline block and above-the-fold copy for an advertorial that will receive cold paid traffic.

cards.title: Handling Objections Before the Sales Page
cards.summary: Shift the norm from FAQ-based objection handling to pre-handling objections inside the advertorial itself.
cards.use_when: Structuring advertorial narrative for a high-consideration or price-sensitive product where prospects arrive skeptical.

cards.title: Choosing Markets and Angles You're Willing to Sell To
cards.summary: The presenter's rule on avoiding price-driven audiences and reframing around premium positioning, plus how to repurpose the resulting angle insight.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build an advertorial offer for a market whose dominant desire is lowest price.

cards.title: Keeping Foundational Documents Reusable Across Copy Assets
cards.summary: Treat the research doc, avatar sheet, offer brief and necessary beliefs as a persistent brand asset set that powers all future AI copy.
cards.use_when: Scaling content production across advertorials, VSLs, ads and landing pages for an existing product or brand.

cards.title: Build the Business Case for Speed with Conversion and Bounce Benchmarks
cards.summary: Use load-time thresholds and revenue math to justify speed work on PDPs, category pages and checkout to stakeholders.
cards.use_when: You need to prioritize a speed initiative against other roadmap items and must translate load time into revenue impact for merchandising, PDP or category page work.

cards.title: Adopt Google Core Web Vitals Thresholds as Speed Targets
cards.summary: Set TTFB, FID and FCP targets from source-cited Google benchmarks and check current averages before optimizing.
cards.use_when: You are setting performance budgets or audit criteria for PDP, category and landing page templates and need concrete numbers.

cards.title: Prioritize the Product and Category Templates Most Shopper Time Spends On
cards.summary: PDPs and category pages carry 72% of page views, so optimize those templates first and quantify time saved per journey.
cards.use_when: You must decide which templates to make faster first with limited engineering capacity.

cards.title: Diagnose and Prepare for IT Brownouts During High-Traffic Sales
cards.summary: High traffic causes dynamic-area slowdowns (cart, login, search), not just crashes; mitigate with queueing and load planning.
cards.use_when: You are planning a flash sale, Black Friday event or product drop and need to protect cart, checkout and login reliability.

cards.title: Set Mobile-Specific Speed Standards Separate from Desktop
cards.summary: Mobile pages load far slower and have higher bounce, so judge speed on mobile metrics and set mobile-specific thresholds.
cards.use_when: You are auditing storefront performance or setting pass/fail thresholds for a mobile-first audience.

cards.title: Reduce Page Weight and Third-Party Script Load to Cut Load Time
cards.summary: Compression and script discipline are constrained by known page-weight and script-cost figures you can plan against.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to prune scripts or compress media as part of a speed budget for PDPs and landing pages.

cards.title: Convert Speed Work from Low Priority into an Urgent Initiative
cards.summary: Marketers recognize speed matters but rarely prioritize it; use the priority gap to frame and defend the case.
cards.use_when: You are trying to get engineering time approved for speed work against feature and animation projects on the roadmap.

cards.title: Model Load-Time Revenue Impact Before and After Speed Fixes
cards.summary: Estimate revenue upside by applying the source's conversion lift to your own sessions, conversion rate and AOV.
cards.use_when: You need a defensible number to decide whether speed work is worth the engineering investment for your funnel.

cards.title: Use Load-Time Tiers to Predict Bounce and Browsing Depth
cards.summary: Load-time bands correlate with predictable bounce-rate and pages-per-session shifts, useful for setting speed SLAs.
cards.use_when: You are setting load-time SLAs or diagnosing why bounce and session depth move, and need reference bands.

cards.title: Translate a Slow Site's Behavioral Damage into Retention and Word-of-Mouth Risk
cards.summary: Quantify how slow pages deter purchases, repeat visits and referrals, not just immediate bounces.
cards.use_when: You are making the retention and brand case for speed to leadership, beyond single-session conversion.

cards.title: Speed Fix Priority Ladder: Images, Scripts, Hosting
cards.summary: A prioritized three-step order for ecommerce speed work: compress images to WebP, cut unused third-party apps/scripts, then upgrade hosting and add a CDN.
cards.use_when: You are deciding where to spend limited dev or app budget on store speed and need the highest-impact fixes first.

cards.title: Core Web Vitals Thresholds and What Each Metric Means for Your Store
cards.summary: Plain definitions and target thresholds for LCP, INP and CLS, mapped to the specific ecommerce elements (hero images, add-to-cart clicks, cookie banners) that drive each metric.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing why a product, category or homepage scores poorly and need to know which CWV metric each page element is hurting.

cards.title: Lighthouse vs PageSpeed Insights: Which Lab Test to Trust
cards.summary: The two tools use the same engine but differ in data source — Lighthouse is a simulated lab test, PageSpeed Insights layers in 28 days of real Chrome user data (CrUX).
cards.use_when: You are interpreting a speed report and need to know whether a score reflects simulated conditions or actual customer experience.

cards.title: Image Optimization That Actually Moves LCP
cards.summary: Format, compression and lazy-loading rules for product photos and hero banners, including the specific threshold and the above-the-fold exception that trips stores up.
cards.use_when: You are preparing product imagery, category banners or a homepage hero and need file-size, format and loading rules that protect LCP.
